messages:
alex.k: Heads-up — noticed 99th% token latency climb in eu-west ~22:00 UTC after the prefill heuristic change. Spikes align with cross-region warmup bursts. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/allocs/alloc-latency?orgId=1

sophia: ugh, saw that too. percentiles jump from ~120ms to ~420ms for a short window. Mostly on dedicated slices that got prefilled from us-east.

lee: Are these the "aggressive-prefill" jobs? I thought we had a region affinity flag.

alex.k: It's the new prefill driver — we relaxed affinity to reduce cold-starts but it appears to be oversubscribing eu-west egress. Warm pools are being backfilled across AZs.

tanvi: can we throttle cross-region prefill? maybe add a soft cap per rack/az to protect local egress bandwidth.

ops-bot: alert: egress-saturation-eu-west threshold breached (5m average) — auto-throttle engaged for non-critical prefill flows.

lee: Quick mitigation: set prefills.source_strategy = "local-first" and reduce prefill_concurrency from 8 -> 3 for eu-west. Small change, low risk.

alex.k: agrees. Also proposing lowering the warmup_threshold from 75% to 50% tokens for dedicated pools for 24h to see effect.

Sophia: (typo) s/sophia/Sophia/ — will run canary in eu-west-staging first.

lee: Command I used in staging:```
./prefillctl set --region eu-west --strategy local-first --concurrency 3
./poolctl update --pool dedicated-eu-west --warmup-threshold 50
```

tanvi: Add an egress token bucket on the prefill proxy too, something like `rate=80MB/s burst=160MB` for region-crossing flows. We used a similar knob in apac.

alex.k: Good call. If we cap cross-region prefill egress we'll avoid saturating NIC queues that cause tail latency regressions for tenants.

ops-bot: deployment:pre-fill-driver v2.3.1 rolled to eu-west-staging at 1805559988 by lee — status: running

Sophia: After staging run (45m): latency tail improved ~60% and prefill completion slowed a bit but still within SLA. No tenant errors.

lee: Plan: 1) push local-first + concurrency=3 to eu-west canary 2) apply egress token bucket on proxy 3) monitor 99th% and tenant error rates for 2h 4) if stable, roll to prod with 30m blast radius

tanvi: who wants to own the blast? alex?

alex.k: I'll own monitoring and rollback. If we see any tenant errors > 0.5% we abort and revert the prefill knob.

Sophia: I'll handle the proxy token-bucket change and metric dashboards. Putting a short runbook in #runbooks after we validate.

lee: ping me once canary is green, I'll prepare the rollout job.

alex.k: thx. also noting cost angle — cross-region prefills add egress charge; if this becomes default we should quantify monthly delta. I'll add a quick estimate after rollout.

tanvi: please also add a short note for product/ops to explain why we tightened prefill heuristics (latency + cost).

alex.k: will do. TL;DR: revert aggressive cross-region prefill, enforce local-first + egress cap, monitor 2h, then roll.

Sophia: 👍 updating staging checklist now.

lee: leaving a snippet for the rollout job (for visibility):```
- canary: 10%
- region: eu-west
- rollback_if: tenant_error_rate > 0.5% OR 99th_percentile_latency > baseline*1.5
- post-check: egress_throughput per-proxy < 80MB/s
```

alex.k: great. tagging ops-oncall to watch the window: @tanvi @lee @sophia. I'll update this thread with go/no-go.

ops-bot: incident-sla-check scheduled: 1805560200 -> 1805563800

Sophia: go for canary in 10m unless any objections.

lee: no objections. go ahead.

alex.k: launching canary now. will update in ~15m.
